page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.64-512 represents a large-scale memory-optimized virtual machine configuration within the Ampere A1 Flex family. Based on the 64-bit ARM architecture, the instance incorporates 64 dedicated Ampere Altra physical cores clocked at a consistent 3.0 GHz. Unlike platforms employing simultaneous multithreading, each vCPU maps directly to a discrete physical core with one thread per core, ensuring consistent computational throughput and preventing sibling thread contention.

System memory is configured at 512 GB, yielding an allocation of 8 GB of RAM per dedicated core. This memory-to-core ratio accommodates demanding memory-bound workloads. In terms of secondary storage and hardware acceleration, the instance includes no local storage drives and zero GPUs, meaning persistent file systems must be supplied via attached cloud block storage volumes. Network configuration provides one complimentary public IPv4 address for external routing.

By leveraging Ampere Altra silicon, this instance provides high core density and massive RAM capacity with favorable power and architectural cost efficiency compared to legacy x86 architectures. It is well suited for memory-intensive enterprise software, large in-memory key-value databases, big data analytics engines, container orchestration nodes, and continuous integration environments targeting ARM64 binaries.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.64-512 is an enterprise-scale memory-optimized virtual instance built on the 64-bit ARM architecture. Powered by 64 dedicated physical Ampere Altra cores operating at a sustained 3.0 GHz clock rate, the instance assigns one thread per core, mitigating thread contention issues typical of hyperthreaded systems. The configuration includes 512 GB of system memory, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-heavy deployments. The instance does not feature bundled local storage disks or hardware GPU acceleration, requiring network-attached block volumes for persistent data needs. An included public IPv4 address provides network reachability. With its dense core count, high memory footprint, and architectural efficiency, this server profile offers cost-effective execution for large-scale in-memory databases, data analytics, container orchestration nodes, and distributed ARM-native compilation pipelines.
